text:
Florida generated more dangerous chances than Minnesota at even strength and lost 4-1 anyway. The deserved-to-win split was 56 percent for FLA and 44 percent for MIN, and the best evidence for it was in the crease. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 29 of 30 shots against 3.19 expected goals for FLA, saving 2.19 goals more than that workload deserved. Jacob Markstrom allowed three on 2.84 expected, roughly what the chances called for.

Minnesota's first goal showed how the night would go. Matt Boldy scored 53 seconds in on a snap shot that carried a 5 percent chance, and Kirill Kaprizov made it 2-0 on a power play at 6:18 of the first. Matthew Tkachuk got one back early in the second, but Kaprizov answered at 5:00 off a Boldy assist, and FLA never pulled closer. Eetu Luostarinen's 21 percent look in the first period was the best chance that didn't go in, and Wallstedt turned it away. FLA also went 0 for 5 on the power play, on 1.28 expected goals.

The third period is where the score got its shape. MIN's expected goals jumped to 2.94 against 1.47 for FLA, and Kaprizov finished the night with a hat trick, the last goal at 18:56 on a 55 percent chance. He ended with three goals and an assist, and Minnesota had 3.52 expected goals with him on the ice against 0.46. The even-strength totals (MIN 1.99, FLA 1.85) say the game was close until then.
